limitations: The DeepThought declaration graph was consulted for the three relevant files. Its declaration locations were verified against source and the TypeScript compiler parser; the visit declarations at lines 202 and 252 are overload signatures, and line 261 is their implementation. Behavioral conclusions below come from source, not declaration relationships. No repository modules, builds or tests were executed.

Compatibility assessment: both validation paths already compose rule visitors into one outer AST walk. Executable validation uses visitWithTypeInfo(typeInfo, visitInParallel(...)); SDL validation uses visitInParallel directly (src/validation/validate.ts:171-181,193-209). A simple loop forwarding each handler's result to visit would change behavior: skip and break must remain local to each constituent visitor. Even the existing composition does not provide isolated editing passes.

The walker performs depth-first enter/children/leave traversal using QueryDocumentKeys by default or the supplied visitorKeys map. Arrays participate in traversal and callback ancestry but receive no visitor callbacks; null and undefined children are skipped. Callbacks receive node, key, parent, path and ancestors, with the visitor as this. Child-key and array order determine traversal order (src/language/visitor.ts:261-338,367-380).

For the raw walker, undefined continues without a direct replacement; false on enter skips that node's descendants and its leave callback; BREAK is an identity sentinel that exits the whole walk without unwinding ancestor leave callbacks. Other defined results record an edit. An AST-node replacement on enter supplies the children subsequently traversed, without another enter callback for the replacement itself; a non-node result, including null, prevents descent. False on leave is not recorded as a replacement (src/language/visitor.ts:100-101,329-380).

Edits returned through visit use copied arrays and objects as changes propagate upward. Null removes array entries, with offsets accounting for earlier removals; object child properties receive null directly. Leave callbacks see nodes incorporating completed child edits. The walker returns its resulting root rather than mutating the original through this edit mechanism; direct mutation inside callbacks is not prevented (src/language/visitor.ts:287-319,349-365,382-387).

Composition preselects handlers by kind and invokes active visitors in input-array order on both enter and leave; leave order is not reversed. Each callback retains its original visitor as this. Enter false records the current node as that visitor's skip marker, suppressing its descendant callbacks and its own leave callback, then normally clearing the marker when that node is left. BREAK permanently disables only that visitor. Neither signal is forwarded as a global traversal instruction. Leave false is absorbed, so later visitors still run (src/language/visitor.ts:423-475). Separate full-document passes would instead have pass-major ordering; consolidating them can therefore change side-effect and error ordering even when they do not edit.

Editing is a shared control effect: the first defined result other than false or BREAK immediately returns from the composition callback, suppressing remaining visitors for that phase. An enter replacement therefore prevents later visitors from entering either the original node or its replacement, although active visitors can subsequently see replacement descendants and its leave event. Null removal suppresses later enter callbacks and all traversal of that subtree. A leave edit similarly suppresses remaining leave callbacks. This differs from independent passes over either the original document or successively transformed documents (src/language/visitor.ts:446-475,349-359,367-378).

Source-derived edit hazard: skip markers use object identity. If visitor A skips node N and visitor B replaces N, or edits a descendant so that N is copied, the eventual leave node can differ from N and A's marker will not clear. A preceding leave edit can also return before a later visitor's marker is cleared. That visitor can consequently remain suppressed beyond the intended subtree. These cases require explicit compatibility decisions and regression checks; independence under arbitrary edits is not guaranteed by the existing helper (src/language/visitor.ts:292-313,451-456,461-473).

Handler selection gives a kind-specific object precedence over generic enter/leave handlers, including when that object omits one phase. A kind-specific function is enter-only and also suppresses generic leave fallback. Generic handlers apply when neither specific form matches. The walker and composer cache these selections during construction, so replacing this with dynamic lookup could change observable behavior (src/language/visitor.ts:266-269,429-438,499-518).

The TypeInfo wrapper enters type state before invoking the delegated enter handler. Any defined enter result causes it to leave the original node; an AST-node result is then entered as the replacement. Delegated leave runs before typeInfo.leave, keeping current-node type information available to leave callbacks. With the current wrapper outside the composition, a local false or BREAK is consumed by the composer, allowing shared type tracking to continue for other visitors. Preserve this wrapper ordering and verify type state after skips, replacements, removals and sibling transitions (src/utilities/TypeInfo.ts:936-967; src/validation/validate.ts:173-180).

Executable-validation integration must preserve validate's optional diagnostic tracing, default rule list, schema assertion, shared ValidationContext and TypeInfo, and options. Its traversal excludes description children. Errors are reported through context.reportError, which invokes the configured error callback; they are not collected from visitor return values. The default maximum is 100, and an additional report after reaching the limit throws a sentinel that is appended to the returned errors. The walk also catches validationAbortedError by identity and rethrows other exceptions; rule construction occurs before that try block (src/validation/validate.ts:48-57,129-189; src/validation/ValidationContext.ts:77-79).

SDL validation uses specifiedSDLRules, a shared SDLValidationContext containing the optional schema to extend, default traversal keys, and an uncapped error collector, without the executable path's TypeInfo wrapper or catch block (src/validation/validate.ts:193-209). Schema construction and extension reach it through assertValidSDL and assertValidSDLExtension unless assumeValid or assumeValidSDL is true; those wrappers combine error messages into a thrown Error (src/utilities/buildASTSchema.ts:63-68; src/utilities/extendSchema.ts:150-158; src/validation/validate.ts:218-239). The default GraphQL harness uses validate, and the GraphQL pipeline returns validation errors before execution (src/harness.ts:7,50-55; src/graphql.ts:261-295).

One shared outer walk does not eliminate all validation traversal. ValidationContext.getVariableUsages performs a cached auxiliary walk with a separate TypeInfo, while fragment-spread and reference helpers traverse selections and share a fragment-work budget that can throw validationAbortedError. Editing also requires accounting for context.getDocument retaining the original AST and caches keyed by original nodes (src/validation/ValidationContext.ts:65-95,101-166,408-446).

Necessary regression checks include exact enter/leave ordering and callback arguments; generic versus kind-specific handler precedence and this binding; nested skips, resumption at siblings, root skips, enter/leave BREAK and leave false; competing edits, enter/leave replacement, removal, replacement-kind changes, copied ancestors and skip-marker cleanup; unchanged-input identity and edit immutability. Validation checks should compare ordered errors and locations, custom and default rules, description exclusion, TypeInfo-dependent fields/arguments/variables/fragments, error-limit boundaries, abort sentinels and unexpected exceptions, SDL construction/extension and bypass options. NoUnusedFragmentsRule supplies a concrete skip-plus-Document-leave case, and FieldsOnCorrectTypeRule depends on current type state (src/validation/rules/NoUnusedFragmentsRule.ts:54-81; src/validation/rules/FieldsOnCorrectTypeRule.ts:65-98). These checks are recommendations derived from the inspected source, not executed results.
